title: 2026 anaerobic-digestion SR2021 No9 CO2 and methane QA controls

sources.title: SR2021 No 9: on-farm AD facility, including use of resultant biogas - waste recovery operation
SR2021 No 9: on-farm anaerobic digestion facility, including use of resultant biogas – waste recovery operation

facts.source_fact: SR2021 No 9 is for anaerobic-digestion treatment capacity below 100 tonnes of waste or combined waste and non-waste per day.
facts.expected_handling: Check daily treatment capacity before applying this standard rule.

facts.source_fact: The permit allows no more than 35,000 tonnes of waste or combined waste and non-waste to be accepted each year.
facts.expected_handling: Keep the annual acceptance cap distinct from daily treatment capacity.

facts.source_fact: The standard rules do not allow vehicle fuelling stations.
facts.expected_handling: Exclude vehicle-fuelling activity from this permit scope.

facts.source_fact: Biogas or natural-gas combustion appliances under Activity 3 must have total aggregated rated thermal input below 5 MW.
facts.expected_handling: Aggregate relevant appliances before testing the thermal-input limit.

facts.source_fact: Activity 3 combustion is limited to single-fuel use.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat mixed-fuel combustion as automatically covered.

facts.source_fact: Activity 4 allows gas storage, drying, cleaning and upgrading to biomethane within the stated technique restrictions.
facts.expected_handling: Keep gas-treatment techniques inside the permitted activity list.

facts.source_fact: Chemical scrubbing using amine-based solvents or other novel techniques with potential air or water emissions is excluded from the stated upgrading route.
facts.expected_handling: Do not classify excluded chemical-scrubbing techniques as standard-rule compliant.

facts.source_fact: The permit allows injection of upgraded biomethane to the national grid.
facts.expected_handling: Tag grid injection as a permitted downstream use, not an emissions measurement.

facts.source_fact: Separation of CO2 from biomethane upgrading is limited to physical techniques under the standard rules.
facts.expected_handling: Require the treatment technique to match the physical-method restriction.

facts.source_fact: Separated CO2 may be treated and stored to meet food-and-beverage or industrial-grade standards.
facts.expected_handling: Carry the intended CO2 grade/use standard with the treatment record.

facts.source_fact: Auxiliary standby flares are limited to burning surplus biogas during emergencies or maintenance.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat routine disposal flaring as permitted operation.

facts.source_fact: New combustion plant must be notified in writing to the Environment Agency before start-up.
facts.expected_handling: Require pre-start notification provenance for new combustion plant.

facts.source_fact: Operators must plan for reduced gas-grid demand and venting or flaring gas for disposal purposes is not permitted.
facts.expected_handling: Reject routine disposal venting or flaring as a normal contingency.

facts.source_fact: Methane leak detection, programmed routine maintenance inspections and repair must be carried out and recorded.
facts.expected_handling: Require leak-detection and repair records rather than assuming methane control.

facts.source_fact: Permitted CO2-producing biogas-upgrading methods include physical techniques such as membrane separation, adsorption, cryogenic separation, washing, water scrubbing, distillation, compression, condensation, drying and cooling.
facts.expected_handling: Validate the actual upgrading method against the permitted physical-technique set.

facts.source_fact: Treatment must achieve at least an 80% capture rate of recovered carbon dioxide.
facts.expected_handling: Treat 80% as a process capture threshold, not a parcel emission reduction value.

facts.source_fact: Recovered CO2 storage capacity is limited to 250 tonnes at any one time.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the capacity limit to on-site stored CO2 inventory.

facts.source_fact: Routine venting of stored CO2 is not allowed; emergency pressure-release venting must be prevented or minimised where practicable.
facts.expected_handling: Separate routine and emergency venting events.

facts.source_fact: Storage of recovered CO2 is limited to six months before use.
facts.expected_handling: Track storage duration and flag inventory beyond the permitted period.

facts.source_fact: Where CCR or HCR conditions apply, the operator must keep a site-specific decarbonisation-readiness report and review it at intervals not exceeding two years.
facts.expected_handling: Carry the report-review date and readiness basis as permit compliance metadata.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach standard-rule activity, capacity and process-technique boundary.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents applying SR2021 No9 outside its scope.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach the 26 February 2026 rule version and relevant review or storage interval.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents stale or timeless compliance claims.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry Environment Agency source URL and technique/permit provenance.
Do not convert process capture, venting or permit thresholds into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate binding gate.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; control_id={package_id}_{fact_id}_{pattern_id}; each generated row inherits confidence_percent=99 and verification=PASS
